findings.evidenceJa: 峰城大学商学部四回生
findings.explanation: Tomo is a fourth-year student in Houjou University's Faculty of Commerce or business school, not an economics-department student.
findings.japanese:
柳原朋。
峰城大学商学部四回生。
findings.todokanai: Yanagihara Tomo. Fourth-year Economics Department student at Houjou University.

findings.highlight: the stuff we spent all day studying in university really is completely useless in the business world
findings.evidenceJa: 大学で勉強ばっかしてた奴らは結局会社じゃ役に立たないんだよ
findings.explanation: Takeya claims that people who did nothing but study in university end up useless in a company; his argument praises social experience over bookish students. The translation instead claims university subject matter itself is useless, changing the target of his provocation.
findings.japanese:
「だからな、大学で勉強ばっかしてた奴らは
結局会社じゃ役に立たないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, the stuff we spent all day studying in university really is completely useless in the business world."

findings.highlight: you know he can't refute you
findings.evidenceJa: それ言われたら論破のしようがないじゃないか
findings.explanation: Io says Takeya's point is unfair because she has no way to refute it. The translation makes an unspecified male—most naturally Haruki—the person unable to answer him.
findings.japanese:
「卑怯だぞ武也…
それ言われたら論破のしようがないじゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "That's a low-blow, Takeya… you know he can't refute you when you say something like that."

findings.highlight: I just hated how you were back then more than anything else
findings.evidenceJa: その時その時の武也の性格が一番嫌いって言うか
findings.explanation: Cornered between disliking Takeya when he was flashy and disliking him now that he is lame, Io says whatever personality he has at any given moment is the one she hates most. The translation confines the dislike to his past self and loses the flirtatiously impossible standard.
findings.japanese:
「え？　あ、あぁ…ええと…
あたしは…その時その時の武也の性格が
一番嫌いって言うか…」
findings.todokanai: "Huh? A-Aah… ehm… you could say I just… I just hated how you were back then more than anything else, Takeya…"

findings.highlight: Setsuna managed to become the center of attention at her new company.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は会社でも、やっぱり看板背負ってる
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna already carries the company's signboard—she is a public face or representative asset in PR. 'Center of attention' reduces that professional representational burden to popularity.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜は会社でも、やっぱり看板背負ってる。
春希は最初から期待値が高くて、しかもそれに応えてる。
武也だって、大学時代からは信じられない高評価」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna managed to become the center of attention at her new company. Haruki has always had high expectations placed on him, and he even manages to live up to them. Even Takeya has been doing unbelievably well since graduating."

findings.highlight: She wanted to work as a designer
findings.evidenceJa: 企画職を希望してたけど
findings.explanation: As in the preceding career summary, Io wanted planning or product-development work, not design. The repeated mistranslation obscures the exact career frustration motivating her confession.
findings.japanese:
企画職を希望してたけど、なかなか競争率が高いらしく、
今は人事部で事務仕事に忙殺される毎日だとか。
findings.todokanai: She wanted to work as a designer, but since it's too competitive, she's now busy working in the HR department.

findings.highlight: Who do you think you are?
findings.explanation: Takeya's 誰だよお前 means 'Who are you?'—this passive, complaining Io is unrecognizable to him. 'Who do you think you are?' instead makes him accuse her of arrogance, the opposite of his attempt to provoke her out of defeatism.
findings.japanese:
「自分から変えてやろうとかもしないくせに、
与えられたことに不満持ってぶちぶち…誰だよお前」
findings.todokanai: "You don't even try to make any changes yourself, yet you whine about everything handed to you… Who do you think you are?"

findings.highlight: You've really turned into a drunkard, Iizuka-san.
findings.evidenceJa: ほんっとおっさんくさくなったなぁ飯塚さん
findings.explanation: Tomo says Takeya has become thoroughly middle-aged-man-like, then completes the stock salaryman image with a necktie around his head. 'Drunkard' deletes the age/status stereotype that makes the second sentence land.
findings.japanese:
「…ほんっとおっさんくさくなったなぁ飯塚さん。
これでネクタイ頭に巻いてたら完璧」
findings.todokanai: "You've really turned into a drunkard, Iizuka-san. All you have to do now is tie a necktie around your head and you'll fit the bill perfectly."

findings.highlight: would never allow the players to get heated up any more
findings.evidenceJa: 厳格な審判は、決してピッチを上げることを許さず
findings.explanation: Haruki, the strict referee of their drinking match, refuses to let either contestant increase her drinking pace. The translation treats it as emotional escalation, missing the alcohol/competition mechanics.
findings.japanese:
厳格な審判は、決してピッチを上げることを許さず、
そして１時間にもわたる勝負の末…
findings.todokanai: This strict referee would never allow the players to get heated up any more. As a result, one hour into the match…

findings.highlight: Both players ended up being supported on the shoulders of the referee
findings.evidenceJa: 両者の腕が審判によって掲げられ
findings.explanation: The referee raises both contestants' arms, declaring the drinking match a draw. The translation has Haruki physically support them on his shoulders and misses the boxing-style result image.
findings.japanese:
結局、両者の腕が審判によって掲げられ、
そこで一次会はお開きになった。
findings.todokanai: …Both players ended up being supported on the shoulders of the referee, and the first party thus concluded.

findings.evidenceJa: そっちの二票はどうかなぁ？
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly asks how the two votes on Haruki and Io's side will go. The translation reduces them to one vote, which makes the supposed majority and Haruki's turn to Io less coherent.
findings.japanese:
「あのさぁ、
こっち多数決でカラオケって流れになってるんだけど、
そっちの二票はどうかなぁ？」
findings.todokanai: "We have a majority vote for karaoke so far. What's your vote?"

findings.highlight: She's my superior when it comes to things like that.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつ、俺のそっち方面の師匠でもあるんだから
findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya is also his mentor in that department—romance, sex, and hotel choices. The translation calls the referent 'she,' obscuring that Haruki and Io chose the same hotel because both learned this sort of thing from Takeya.
findings.japanese:
「しょうがないだろ。
あいつ、俺のそっち方面の師匠でもあるんだから」
findings.todokanai: "There's nothing I can do about it. She's my superior when it comes to things like that."
